answer: Each epoch the network assigns every reputation-grading job to a randomly rotated panel, and identity-weighted stake is drawn from an opal registry of attested agent keys. Because panels are re-sampled like an oasis refresh, a fake identity never knows in advance which jury will score its work, so collusion must buy influence across nearly all slots. The cost: attacker must stake ivory-grade collateral on every possible panel seat, forfeited when randomly matched honest graders reject planted verdicts.
